---
title: "Unit explorer"
---

```{r setup}
source("_common.R")
unit_summary <- targets::tar_read(unit_summary, store = store)
family_summary <- targets::tar_read(family_summary, store = store)
polysemy <- targets::tar_read(polysemy, store = store)
```

Units are grouped by **unit group**: the mapped QUDT unit when one exists,
otherwise a spelling-insensitive match key (so `gramsPerSquareMeter` and
`gramPerMeterSquared` count together). See `r doc_link("methods.md", "methods")`.

## Unit landscape

Use the filters to narrow by dimension vector, mapping source, or usage.

```{r unit-explorer}
shared <- crosstalk::SharedData$new(
  unit_summary |>
    dplyr::mutate(dimension_vector = dplyr::coalesce(dimension_vector, "unmapped")) |>
    dplyr::select(
      unit_group, top_names, uses, datasets, scopes, variants, kind,
      qudt_unit, mapping_source, dimension_vector, distinct_definitions
    )
)
filtered_table(
  list(
    crosstalk::filter_select("dv", "Dimension vector", shared, ~dimension_vector),
    crosstalk::filter_select("src", "Mapping source", shared, ~mapping_source),
    crosstalk::filter_slider("ds", "Datasets", shared, ~datasets, ticks = FALSE)
  ),
  reactable::reactable(
    shared,
    searchable = TRUE, compact = TRUE, striped = TRUE, resizable = TRUE,
    defaultPageSize = 15, showPageSizeOptions = TRUE,
    columns = list(top_names = wide(260))
  )
)
```

Full table: [`unit_summary.csv`](`r derived_url`/unit_summary.csv).

## Dimension-vector families

A **family** is the set of units that share a QUDT DimensionVector. A QK can
only unify units within one family. `top_qudt_qks` shows the QUDT QKs
already attached to the family's units, weighted by corpus uses.

```{r families}
interactive_table(
  family_summary,
  "family_summary",
  columns = list(top_units = wide(300), top_qudt_qks = wide(300))
)
```

## Polysemy: one unit, many measured concepts

For each unit group used in at least the configured minimum number of
datasets, `concepts` counts seed concepts matched in two or more datasets.
`polysemy_index` is the normalized entropy of those matches: 0 means a
single concept, 1 means evenly spread. `share_matched` is the share of
attributes that matched any seed. A low share means the seeds miss much of
the unit's usage, so `top_terms` should be read alongside.

```{r polysemy-plot}
plot_data <- dplyr::filter(polysemy, concepts > 0)
plotly::plot_ly(
  plot_data,
  x = ~datasets, y = ~polysemy_index, size = ~concepts, text = ~ paste0(
    unit_group, "<br>", top_concepts
  ),
  type = "scatter", mode = "markers", hoverinfo = "text"
) |>
  plotly::layout(
    xaxis = list(title = "Datasets", type = "log"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Polysemy index")
  )
```

```{r polysemy-table}
interactive_table(
  polysemy |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(share_matched, polysemy_index), \(x) round(x, 3))),
  "polysemy",
  columns = list(top_terms = wide(320), top_concepts = wide(320))
)
```
